result.direction: Direction 2 (label: sphere): the minimal winding of self-similar three-vortex collapse on the sphere. The work defines the rotation about the collision point, finds how it depends on size relative to the radius, and asks whether the planar bound P > sqrt(3)/2 carries over.
result.summary:
On the unit sphere, take circulations with M = sum_{i<j} Gamma_i Gamma_j = 0 and L = sum_{i<j} Gamma_i Gamma_j l_ij^2 = 0 (l_ij are chord lengths). The collision point is p = J/S, where J = sum Gamma_i x_i and S = sum Gamma_i. It is a unit vector and always lies on the circumcircle of the vortex triangle.

The main result is proved. The sphere velocity splits exactly into two parts: cos(beta) times the planar Biot-Savart velocity of the chord triangle in its own plane, plus a tilt of that plane. Here beta is the angular radius of the circumcircle, measured from its pole n. At every instant the motion is a similarity about p. The chords shrink at cos(beta) times the planar rate of the same chord triangle, but the rotation about p is exactly the planar rate, Im kappa. So n.p = cos(beta) grows linearly in time, and the rotation angle is psi = (bhat/ahat) ln tan(beta/2) + const. The pole n, which is the spherical circumcenter, therefore runs along a loxodrome with poles at p and -p. It crosses every meridian at the constant angle arctan(2 P0), where P0 is the planar winding of the chord shape. Every motion is one full loxodrome: a burst from p, a great-circle state, then collapse back at the same point p.

The ledger says no single rotation rate exists on the sphere. That is only half right. Individual azimuthal rates about p do differ, and I derive the difference in closed form, but there is a single canonical rotation rate.

How much the configuration winds depends on how size is measured:
- Per unit ln(chord^2): P0/sqrt(1 - rho_c^2/R^2), where rho_c is the triangle's Euclidean circumradius and R the sphere radius. This goes to infinity at the great circle.
- Per remaining time, omega*(t_c - t): P0 sec^2(beta/2).
- As the pitch of the pole's loxodrome: exactly P0 at every size.
Because the curvature factor does not depend on shape, the planar theorem transfers directly. The bound sqrt(3)/2 still holds, and it gets stronger with size for the first two measures, sharply: (sqrt3/2) sec(beta) and (sqrt3/2) sec^2(beta/2). For each fixed mu, the planar minimizing shape is the minimizer at every size.

Two secondary results. Proved: each vortex's path exceeds twice its initial chord distance to p. Numerical evidence only: it also exceeds twice the geodesic distance, although for a given shape the geodesic ratio can fall below its planar value.

Checks: exact SymPy identities; the sphere Biot-Savart at 360 random configurations (50 digits, residuals up to 1.5e-47); and a 45-digit Taylor integration through the great-circle state that matches the laws to about 1e-39 absolute or better.

results.statement: Setup: unit sphere, velocities dx_i/dt = (1/2pi) sum_j Gamma_j (x_j x x_i)/|x_i - x_j|^2, M = 0, L = 0, not a relative equilibrium. Let p = J/S, n = the unit normal of the plane Pi through x1, x2, x3 (oriented by the triangle), d = n.p, rho = sqrt(1-d^2), c = d n, a = (p-c)/rho, b' = n x a. Let kappa = alpha + i beta_k be the common planar ratio u_i/(x_i - p) of the chord triangle in Pi, with orientation n, and put ahat = rho^2 alpha, bhat = rho^2 beta_k. These depend only on the chord shape. Then: (a) |p| = 1, p lies in Pi, and so p lies on the circumcircle of the triangle. (b) For every i, dx_i/dt = s (x_i - p) + Omega x (x_i - p), with s = d alpha and Omega = d beta_k n + rho (beta_k a - alpha b'). (c) Consequently the chord shape is constant; dn/dt = -rho(alpha a + beta_k b'); d(n.p)/dt = -ahat, which is constant; Omega.p = beta_k; and the azimuthal rate of n about p is exactly beta_k = bhat/rho^2. In words: the chords shrink at cos(beta) times the planar rate of the same chord triangle, but the rotation about p is not slowed at all.
results.evidence: Proof. (a) |J|^2 = S^2 - L, and p = sum (Gamma_i/S) x_i is an affine combination of the x_i. (b) First write x_j x x_i = d (x_j - x_i) x n + (x_j - x_i) x (x_i - c). The first term gives d times the planar velocity u_i. The second is normal to Pi, equal to nu_i n. For any three points in a plane, (1/2pi) sum Gamma_j [(xi_j - xi_i) x xi_i].n/|xi_i - xi_j|^2 = -u_i.xi_i (identity N, a complex-number identity), so nu_i = -u_i.(x_i - c). The planar theory gives u_i = alpha w_i + beta_k n x w_i with w_i = x_i - p, because L = 0 and M = 0 give planar self-similarity, with p as the planar center of vorticity. Substituting and using |w|^2 = -2 rho w.a on the circle gives the stated s and Omega. (c) The 4-point set {x_i, p} therefore moves by similarities fixing p. The normal is carried by the rotation, dn/dt = Omega x n. Taking components along p and e_perp finishes the proof. There is no division by d, so all of this holds through d = 0. Exact check: sympy_identities.py verifies identity N and every frame identity in (b) and (c), each giving exactly 0. Numerical check: check_static.py builds 180 configurations from the paper's planar parametrization with random mu, theta and d in (-1,1). Self-similarity residual <= 2.2e-50, s <= 9e-51, Omega.p <= 1.2e-49, d n.p/dt <= 1.5e-49, psi-dot <= 9e-50, at 50 digits. check_independent.py places 180 configurations directly on the sphere: x1, x2 random, x3 on the L = 0 circle of the sphere, nothing planar used in the construction. Planar kappa is computed separately by planar Biot-Savart in the chord plane. Errors: |p|-1 <= 5e-51, p in plane <= 3e-51, n.p rate <= 1e-49, psi-dot <= 7e-50, chord rates <= 1.5e-47. results.statement: Loxodrome law. Let beta in (0, pi) be the angle between p and the pole n_c = sign(-ahat) n; this is the angular radius of the circumcircle, measured from the pole that moves toward p. Then: (i) cos beta = 1 - |ahat| (t_c - t). Equivalently the chord distance from the spherical circumcenter to p satisfies |n_c - p|^2 = |n_c(0) - p|^2 (1 - t/t_c), exactly the planar law, and the spherical-cap area 2 pi R^2 (1 - cos beta) falls linearly at the rate 2 pi |ahat|, which is the planar circumdisk rate. (ii) The azimuth of n_c about p is psi = -2 P0 ln tan(beta/2) + const, with P0 = |bhat|/(2|ahat|) the planar winding of the chord shape. So n_c moves on the loxodrome (rhumb line) with poles -p and p. It crosses every meridian at the constant angle arctan(2 P0), the planar spiral angle. In the stereographic chart from -p its image 2 tan(beta/2) e^{i psi} is an exact logarithmic spiral with the planar exponent. (iii) Every self-similar motion is one full loxodrome from n_c = -p to n_c = p: a burst from p, then a great-circle state (beta = pi/2, all chords stationary, maximal size rho_c = R), then collapse at the same point p. The lifetime is 2 R^2/|ahat|, and the time from angle beta to collapse is R^2 (1 - cos beta)/|ahat|. The total rotation diverges logarithmically at both ends. Relative to the planar spiral of the same chord shape, collapsing from angle beta0 adds 2 P0 ln(2/(1 + cos beta0)) of extra rotation.
results.evidence: From S1(c): d(cos beta)/dt = |ahat| and dpsi/dt = bhat/sin^2 beta. So dpsi/dbeta = (bhat/ahat)/sin beta, which integrates to psi = (bhat/ahat) ln tan(beta/2). For a curve on the sphere, the tangent of its angle to the meridian is sin(beta) |dpsi/dbeta| = 2 P0, which is constant; this is the definition of a loxodrome. Stereographic projection is conformal and maps meridians to rays, so the image is a log spiral. The burst and collapse points coincide because J = S p is conserved. results.statement: Winding on the sphere of radius R, with rho_c the Euclidean circumradius of the vortex triangle and K = 1/R^2: (1) per unit ln(chord^2): |dpsi/d ln l_ij^2| = P0 |sec beta| = P0/sqrt(1 - K rho_c^2), the same for every pair and in both phases. It varies along the motion, from P0 at collapse to infinity at the great-circle state. (2) Time-based: |omega(t)| (t_c - t) = P0 sec^2(beta/2), which in the final phase (beta <= pi/2) equals 2 P0/(1 + sqrt(1 - K rho_c^2)) and lies in (P0, 2 P0]. (3) Loxodrome pitch of the pole = P0 exactly. Chord shapes of spherical collapses are exactly the planar zero-impulse shapes, excluding the collinear ones, and the curvature factors depend only on beta. So the planar theorem transfers: for every self-similar collapse on the sphere, at every instant, (1) > (sqrt3/2)/sqrt(1 - K rho_c^2), (2) > sqrt3/(1 + sqrt(1 - K rho_c^2)) in the final phase, and (3) > sqrt3/2. Each bound is sharp for every fixed size (infimum as mu -> 0, not attained). For fixed mu the minima P_-(mu) sec beta, and so on, are attained, by the planar minimizing shape at every size. The planar bound therefore persists. It strengthens with the size-to-radius ratio for measures (1) and (2) and is unchanged for (3). Example: at the chord size where rho_c = R/2 (beta = 30 degrees), the sharp floors are 1 and 0.9282.
results.evidence: Measure (1) follows from S2: dpsi/d ln sin^2 beta = (bhat/ahat)/(2 cos beta), and every l_ij is proportional to sin beta. Measure (2): omega = bhat/sin^2 beta and t_c - t = (1 - cos beta)/|ahat| give 2 P0/(1 + cos beta). The bounds follow from S1, S2 and the paper's Theorem 1 and Corollary 1 (P0 >= P_-(mu) > sqrt3/2, sharp). A chord triangle of any circumradius rho_c <= R can be placed on the sphere with either sign of d, and S1 shows its motion is self-similar. So for each fixed beta the set of achievable P0 is exactly the planar set. Table of values: table.py. The formulas are the ones verified numerically in S1 and S2; the derivative of psi with respect to ln chord^2 comes from the verified psi(beta) law to 1e-40.
results.novelty_risk: These are corollaries of S1 and S2 plus the planar theorem, so their novelty is the novelty of S1 and S2 together with the planar bound, whose priority the paper itself leaves unconfirmed. I found no spherical winding bound in any accessible source. The RESEARCH.md skip entries concern hunting for new 'omega t_c' identities around Kidambi-Newton; I ran only a handful of summary-level searches to assess novelty and re-derived nothing that the ledger marks as done.

results.statement: The individual vortex azimuthal rates about p differ; the ledger/KN observation is correct. In closed form: dphi_j/dt = bhat/rho^2 - ahat sin(sig_j/2) cos(sig_j/2)/(d^2 sin^2(sig_j/2) + cos^2(sig_j/2)), where sig_j is the fixed central angle of vortex j from p on the circumcircle. Equivalently tan(phi_j - psi) = -cot(sig_j/2)/d. The common part is the canonical rotation rate psi-dot = Omega.p. The extra terms stay bounded while psi-dot blows up as 1/rho^2, so every per-vortex winding rate per ln chord^2 tends to P0 at collapse. Consequently the ledger's statement that 'a single omega t_c is not defined on the sphere' should be refined: a canonical omega exists, and omega (t_c - t) = P0 sec^2(beta/2).
results.evidence: The vortex positions are x_j = R_p(psi) Std_j(d), with the standard position computed in the frame (e, e_perp, p). The rate follows by differentiating atan2(-cos(sig/2), d sin(sig/2)) and using d(d)/dt = -ahat. Checked against sphere Biot-Savart at 540 vortex instances in check_independent.py: max relative error 1.2e-49 at 50 digits.

results.statement: Path length of vortex j from pole angle beta0 to collapse: path_j = (W_j |khat|/|ahat|) E(beta0 | m_j), an incomplete elliptic integral of the second kind, with W_j = 2 sin(sig_j/2), m_j = K_j^2/|khat|^2 and K_j = bhat sin(sig_j/2) + ahat cos(sig_j/2). Consequently path_j >= r_j sqrt(1 + 4 P0^2) > 2 r_j, where r_j is the initial chord distance from vortex j to p. So the planar statement that each vortex travels more than twice its initial distance persists on the sphere with chord distance, with the same sharp constant 2.
results.evidence: The speed is |dx_j/dt|^2 = W_j^2 (|khat|^2/rho^2 - K_j^2), from S1(b). This formula was checked against Biot-Savart at 540 instances, max relative error 4.8e-49 (check_independent.py). Since K_j^2 <= |khat|^2, the speed is at least W_j |khat| |d|/rho. With dt = dd/|ahat|, integrating gives at least W_j rho0 |khat|/|ahat| = r_j sqrt(1 + 4 P0^2); when d0 < 0 the integral is larger still. Sharpness: as mu -> 0 with d0 -> 1 the ratio tends to 2 (pathlength.py).
results.novelty_risk: The elliptic-integral form and the chord bound were not found in the sources. The bound is a direct corollary of the planar sqrt(3)/2 theorem combined with S1.

result.depth_assessment:
This is a clean structural result of moderate depth. The key mechanism is elementary once it is seen: the sphere velocity equals cos(beta) times the planar velocity of the chord triangle, plus a tilt that exactly restores the planar rotation about p. The consequences are sharp and not obvious: a canonical rotation rate exists despite the distinct individual azimuthal speeds, the circumcircle's pole moves on a loxodrome with exactly the planar pitch, and the winding depends on size through the explicit factors sec(beta) or sec^2(beta/2).

The answer to the stated question is definitive and proved. The planar bound persists. It strengthens with the size-to-radius ratio for the chord-based and time-based measures, sharply and with a curvature-independent minimizing shape, and it is unchanged for the loxodrome pitch.

There are limits on what is new. No new minimization was needed: the bounds are corollaries of the planar theorem, because the curvature factor does not depend on shape. Part of the setting is known, namely the chord-length law, the burst-equator-collapse picture and the partner-state collapse times (Borisov-Lebedev 1998, Kidambi-Newton 1998/1999). Priority for the rotation and loxodrome results cannot be confirmed, because the Kidambi-Newton full texts were blocked by the egress policy.

result.direction: n-vortex: Is there a universal lower bound on the winding P = |omega_0| t_c for self-similar collapse of N >= 4 point vortices? Does collapse have to rotate?
result.summary: The three-vortex bound P > sqrt(3)/2 does not carry over to more vortices. For N = 4 the minimum of P is P_4 = 0.797896783879863480767605871821495101655536310383..., reached at a non-degenerate configuration. It is a strict local minimum (positive Hessian on the tangent space of the solution manifold), and the numerical evidence says it is the global minimum for N = 4: over 220 independent descents all end there, and 0 of 4500 random Newton starts find any solution at P = 0.797, against 1595 of 3000 at P = 0.799. The minimizer is one strong vortex near the collision point plus a weak cluster of three vortices. The best minimum found falls further as N grows: N=5 0.744814..., N=6 0.713680..., N=7 0.693662, N=8 0.679770, N=9 0.659260, N=11 0.617951..., N=13 0.591860..., N=21 0.542907..., N=29 0.523221 (certified), N=31 0.520016 (float64 KKT). From about N=9 upward the best configurations are two-armed: a central positive vortex, two strong negative vortices, and an S-shaped chain of positive vortices that looks like a discretized vortex sheet. The one-arm family extrapolates to about 0.604 and the two-arm family to about 0.4775. So the infimum over all N is at most 0.5200 and probably about 0.477; whether it is 0 is still open. On rotation I proved an exact formula for any self-similar motion: Im kappa = (Gamma_tot*sigma(w) - L)/(4 pi |v|^2) and Re kappa = v^T E(w) Gamma/(4 pi |v|^2), where v = (I+D)^{-1}s depends only on the shape. So collapse without rotation is impossible exactly when the purely geometric number sigma(w) = 1^T(I+D)^{-1}s is nonzero. I conjecture sigma > 0 for every set of distinct points, which would mean every self-similar collapse rotates in the direction of its total circulation. I have proved that only for N=2 and for three points on a line through the origin; it is heavily supported numerically. Finally, the three-vortex infimum sqrt(3)/2 has a simple origin: it is the limit of a strong vortex with a weak dipole orbiting it, where P = (2+cos 2gamma)/(2 sin 2gamma) with minimum sqrt(3)/2. For N = 4 that limit is not a minimum: P decreases linearly away from it into the interior.

results.statement: Take N point vortices, not all at one point, with Gamma_tot != 0, in self-similar motion zdot_j = kappa w_j, where w_j = z_j - z_c and s_j = |w_j|^2. Define the real antisymmetric N x N matrices D and E by D_jk + i E_jk = (w_j + w_k)/(w_j - w_k) for j != k (so D_jk = (s_j - s_k)/|w_j - w_k|^2), with zero diagonals. Let v = (I+D)^{-1} s, sigma(w) = sum_j v_j and L = sum_j Gamma_j s_j. Then 4 pi |v|^2 Im kappa = Gamma_tot sigma(w) - L and 4 pi |v|^2 Re kappa = v^T E Gamma. In particular every collapse or expansion (L = 0) satisfies Im kappa = Gamma_tot sigma(w)/(4 pi |v|^2) and P = |Gamma_tot| sigma / (2 |v^T E Gamma|). So a self-similar collapse without rotation exists if and only if some collapsing configuration has sigma(w) = 0.
results.evidence: Proof: Biot-Savart gives conj(kappa) conj(w_j) = (1/2 pi i) sum_k Gamma_k/(w_j - w_k). Multiply by 2 pi i w_j and use w_j/(w_j - w_k) = (1 + K_jk)/2, where K = D + iE. This gives 4 pi i conj(kappa) s = Gamma_tot 1 - (I - K) Gamma, which also holds trivially for a vortex at z_c. The real part is (I - D) Gamma = Gamma_tot 1 - 4 pi Im kappa s; the imaginary part is E Gamma = 4 pi Re kappa s. Since D is antisymmetric, x^T (I + D) x = |x|^2, so I + D is invertible and v^T s = |v|^2 > 0. Also v^T (I - D) Gamma = ((I + D) v)^T Gamma = s^T Gamma = L. Taking the inner product of both equations with v gives the formulas. If Re kappa != 0, the Gamma-weighted sum of the equations gives sum_{i<j} GiGj = 2 pi (Im kappa + i Re kappa) L, hence L = 0, sum GiGj = 0, and Gamma_tot^2 = |Gamma|^2 > 0. Numerical check: at 40 digits the formula reproduces kappa computed directly from Biot-Savart to 20+ digits for the N = 4, 5, 11 and 25 minimizers (check_formula.py).
results.novelty_risk: The algebra is elementary, so a version could exist in O'Neil (Trans. AMS 302, 1987), who converted collapse equations to polynomial systems, or in the general N-vortex part of Gotoda (J. Dyn. Differ. Equ. 33, 2021). Neither was checked for N >= 4: both hosts were blocked, and the ledger records reading only Gotoda Section 3. The reduction of 'collapse must rotate' to the sign of one geometric scalar was not found in any source consulted.

results.statement: Conjecture: sigma(w) = 1^T (I + D)^{-1} s > 0 for every N >= 2 and every set of distinct points w_j in C, with s_j = |w_j|^2 and D_jk = (s_j - s_k)/|w_j - w_k|^2. A stronger form: sigma * det(I - D) >= sum_j s_j, with equality exactly for co-circular points. By R3 this implies that every self-similar collapse of point vortices rotates, and in the direction of its total circulation: sign(Im kappa) = sign(Gamma_tot). That would answer question (d) in general.
results.evidence: Proved for N = 2, from the identity sigma (1 + delta^2) = s1 + s2 + (s1 - s2)^2/d^2 with delta = D12. Proved for any three points on a line through the origin: sigma = [sum_j x_j^2 prod_{k != j}(x_j - x_k)] / [(1/2) sum_{i<j}(x_i - x_j)^2], which is the degree-2 Schur sum and is nonnegative for all reals. For N = 3 self-similar configurations it follows from the paper's Im kappa > 0. Numerically: 120,000 random configurations (N = 3..12) have min sigma/sum(s) > 0. Adversarial gradient minimization of sigma/sum(s) for N = 3..10 drives it to 1e-16 only when two points collide (relative distance 1e-9 to 1e-12). Minimizing sigma*det(I-D)/sum(s) gives min 1.000 for N = 3, 4, 6, reached at co-circular points, and never below 1. Every self-similar solution found (more than 2000, N = 4, 5, with b in {1.6, 2, 3.4, 4, 5, 10, 20}) has Gamma_tot*Im kappa > 0. For arbitrary positive diagonal S and symmetric C >= 0 the matrix version of sigma can be negative (D = SC - CS is the commutator form, N >= 3), so planar geometry is essential. Several proof attempts failed: symmetric-part PSD after diagonal congruence, layer-cake on tail sums, and sign-definite v. Scripts: sigma_test.py, sigma_min.py, sigma_adv.py, sigma_sym.py, colsym.py.
results.novelty_risk: For N = 3 the sign of rotation is classical (Groebli, Aref). A general statement that N-vortex collapse must rotate may exist in O'Neil 1987 or later work (unchecked, hosts blocked). WebSearch summaries asserted it but cited no source, which is weak evidence.

results.statement: The three-vortex infimum sqrt(3)/2 is the limit of a strong vortex (circulation 1) orbited by a weak point-vortex dipole (circulations mu and -mu/(1+mu), separation eps -> 0). Use the strong vortex at unit distance as reference, and let gamma be the angle between the dipole axis (from - to +) and the radius vector. At leading order, self-similarity requires mu/eps = -2 cos gamma and gives kappa = (1/2 pi)[-sin 2gamma + i(2 + cos 2gamma)]. Hence P = (2 + cos 2gamma)/(2 sin 2gamma) >= sqrt(3)/2, with equality at cos 2gamma = -1/2 and eps = mu. That is a spiral angle of exactly pi/3.
results.evidence: This is a formal leading-order derivation: center motion equals orbital velocity plus dipole self-propulsion, and relative motion equals the strain of the strong vortex plus the imbalance (mu - mu')/delta with mu - mu' ~ mu^2. The imaginary-part matching condition is then satisfied identically. Checked against the paper's exact formula on arc A_-: at mu = 1e-5 the reduced P(gamma) matches the exact P(theta) to about 1e-10 at 6 points across the arc, with mu/eps = -2 cos gamma to 5e-6. At the exact minimizer, eps/mu -> 1 and cos 2gamma -> -1/2 (to 1e-10 at mu = 1e-5), and P_-(mu) - sqrt(3)/2 ≈ 1.30 mu^2. The limit could be made rigorous from the paper's closed-form P(theta) with theta = pi + mu t; that expansion was not written out.
results.novelty_risk: Possible prior work: dipole-vortex interaction studies such as Lydon-Nazarenko-Laurie, J. Phys. A 55 (2022) 385702 (dipoles meeting clusters, 'time-reversed self-similar collapse'; unread, host blocked) and Leoncini-Kuznetsov-Zaslavsky 2000. The explicit P(gamma) formula and its minimum were not found.

results.statement: For N = 4 the degenerate boundary does not explain the minimum. Constrain the weak cluster to norm eps = ||(Gamma_2, Gamma_3, Gamma_4)||/Gamma_1. The minimal P then decreases roughly linearly from sqrt(3)/2 as eps grows (slope ≈ -0.46): 0.8614 at eps = 0.01, 0.8444 at 0.05, 0.8269 at 0.1, 0.8047 at 0.2. It reaches the interior global minimum 0.797897 at eps ≈ 0.30. In the eps -> 0 limit the triple reduces to the dipole satellite of R6 (P -> sqrt(3)/2). By contrast, for N = 3 the dipole-satellite point is approached quadratically from above (P - sqrt(3)/2 ≈ 1.30 mu^2). That is why sqrt(3)/2 is an infimum for N = 3 but not a lower bound for N >= 4. No descent (over 400 runs for N = 4..7) ended at a degenerate configuration with P < 0.81.
results.evidence: Constrained Levenberg-Marquardt plus descent in b with the extra equation sum_{j>=2} G_j^2 = eps^2 (weakcluster.py, output weak4.out). Float64, residuals < 1e-12. Degenerate endings were recorded in all descent runs (desc*.json).

result.depth_assessment: The most solid result is a negative one: a certified four-vortex counterexample (110 digits, independently validated) showing that sqrt(3)/2 is not a universal lower bound. The evidence that it is the global N=4 minimum is strong but numerical. The exact kappa identity (R3) is elementary but structurally meaningful: it reduces 'must collapse rotate?' to the sign of one explicit geometric scalar sigma(w), and it also explains why the rotation sense follows Gamma_tot. It is not a proof of rotation, because sigma > 0 is proved only for N=2 and for collinear points through the center, and remains a well-supported conjecture otherwise. The large-N picture (one-arm and then two-arm sheet-like minimizers, extrapolated limits about 0.604 and about 0.477) is careful numerics with certified local minima. Global optimality at each N >= 8 is not established, and other structures could do better at large N, so the true infimum over N (positive or 0) is open. The dipole-satellite explanation of sqrt(3)/2 is a clean formal asymptotic confirmed to 1e-10, not a rigorous proof. Main novelty risks: O'Neil RCD 2007 (four-vortex collapse configurations computed at a given velocity ratio) and O'Neil TAMS 1987 / Gotoda 2021 for the identity. Neither could be read from this session.

result.direction: Direction 3 (alpha-models). The kernel is G(r) = r^(-alpha)/(2 pi alpha), normalized so that dz_j/dt = (i/2pi) sum_k Gamma_k |z_j-z_k|^(-alpha-2) (z_j-z_k). alpha -> 0 is the Euler system of the paper and alpha = 1 is SQG. The direction covers self-similar three-vortex collapse: its conditions, a parametrization, the winding number P and its infimum P_min(alpha).
result.summary:
For every alpha >= 0 (in fact every alpha > -0.896), P_min has the closed form sqrt(3+alpha)/(2+alpha), and I proved it with a short elementary argument. The same argument gives a new one-page proof of the paper's Euler bound sqrt(3)/2 that needs no resultants.

Setup. A self-similar motion still has dz/dt = kappa(t)(z - z_c), now with kappa(t) = kappa_0 lambda^-(alpha+2) and lambda^(alpha+2) = 1 + (alpha+2) Re(kappa_0) t. Every vortex still moves on a logarithmic spiral. The rotation per e-fold of size^2 is P = |Im kappa|/(2|Re kappa|). The path therefore meets the direction to the collision point at the angle arctan(2P), and each vortex travels r0 sqrt(1+4P^2) before collapse. The paper's product P = |omega_0| t_c is no longer the same number: it becomes |omega_0| t_c = 2P/(alpha+2).

Conditions. H is homogeneous of degree -alpha, so collapse forces H = 0. The angular-impulse condition does not change: L = 0 as in Euler. Both conditions depend on the shape, so every scalene triangle has exactly one admissible circulation ratio: Gamma_i proportional to r_i^2/(F_k - F_j), with F = r^(-alpha-2) and (i,j,k) cyclic. For each shape, one orientation collapses and the other expands.

Closed form. Im kappa is half the sum of the isolated-pair rotation rates, and P = |sum_cyc r_i^2 coth(beta ln(r_k/r_j))|/(8 Area) with beta = 1 + alpha/2. The circulations drop out of this formula.

Main result. P > sqrt(3+alpha)/(2+alpha), and the constant is sharp but not attained. Equivalently, every vortex travels more than (4+alpha)/(2+alpha) times its initial distance to the collision point, and the spiral angle exceeds arccos((2+alpha)/(4+alpha)). The infimum is approached only in a limit: a weak vortex dipole spiralling into a strong vortex.

Behaviour in alpha. P_min(alpha) decreases strictly: sqrt(3)/2 at alpha = 0 (it is continuous there), 2/3 for SQG, sqrt(5)/4 at alpha = 2, and it tends to 0 as alpha -> infinity. So SQG collapses can wind less than any Euler collapse.

Checks. Formulas were checked against direct Biot-Savart at 40-50 digits, and the collapse law by RK4 integration for four alpha values. Near the limit, P - P_min = c2 rho^2 + c3 rho^(2+alpha) + ..., with exact positive c2 and c3 (rho is the smallest side). A global scan over 45 alpha values is consistent with the proof.

Novelty. The collapse conditions are certainly known. The parametrization and the rate formulas are probably in unread papers (Chen-Liu 2024; JPSJ 90 124401, 2021). The sharp bound and the proof were not found in the searches, but the key full texts are unread and most scholarly hosts were blocked, so that is weak evidence.

results.statement: Self-similar motion in the alpha-model. Suppose dz_j/dt = kappa_0 (z_j - z_c) at t = 0. Then z_j(t) = z_c + lambda e^{i phi}(z_j(0) - z_c), with lambda^(alpha+2) = 1 + (alpha+2) Re(kappa_0) t and phi = (Im kappa_0/Re kappa_0) ln lambda, and kappa(t) = kappa_0 lambda^-(alpha+2). Collapse happens iff Re kappa_0 < 0, at t_c = -1/((alpha+2) Re kappa_0). Every vortex moves on a logarithmic spiral. P := |Im kappa|/(2|Re kappa|) is constant along the motion and is the rotation per e-fold decrease of size^2. The path meets the direction to the collision point at the angle arctan(2P), and the distance travelled to collapse is r0 sqrt(1+4P^2). Also omega(t)(t_c - t) = |omega_0| t_c = 2P/(alpha+2), which is the rotation per e-fold of the remaining time; for alpha > 0 this is not P.
results.evidence: Proof. The Biot-Savart right-hand side is homogeneous of degree -(1+alpha) and rotation-equivariant. Substituting the similarity ansatz gives lambdadot + i lambda phidot = kappa_0 lambda^-(1+alpha). Hence lambda^(alpha+1) lambdadot = Re kappa_0 and dphi/d ln lambda = Im kappa_0/Re kappa_0. The arc length of the log spiral from r0 to 0 is r0 sqrt(1+(Im/Re)^2). Checked by RK4 at 30 digits to t = 0.9 t_c for alpha = 0.5, 1, 1.5 and 1.8 (3000 steps). |z-z_c|/r0 follows lambda to 1e-13, the phase follows (Im/Re) ln lambda to 4e-13, and the angle arctan(2P) holds to 1e-29. Script: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-GENChase/04604b4b-7efe-5ca6-9b53-4838030930e5/scratchpad/research/alpha-models/integrate.py. omega_0 t_c = 2P/(alpha+2) was checked to 15 digits in verify_extremal.py.
results.novelty_risk: Known or elementary. The ledger records Badin-Barry 2018 as identifying log-spiral trajectories, and Grotto-Pappalettera 2025 as giving Z(t) = ((4-a)a(t-t0))^{1/(4-a)} exp(...). Only the definition of P as the per-e-fold pitch is a choice made here.

results.statement: Conditions and parametrization. A self-similar three-vortex collapse requires H = sum Gamma_j Gamma_k r_jk^-alpha = 0 and L = sum Gamma_j |z_j - z_c|^2 = 0. L is unchanged from Euler; H = 0 replaces the harmonic condition. Sum Gamma is automatically nonzero, since sum Gamma = 0 forces a collinear shape. Equivalently, sum_i r_i^2/Gamma_i = 0 and sum_i r_i^-alpha/Gamma_i = 0, where r_i is the side opposite vertex i. For a scalene triangle these hold iff Gamma_i = lam r_i^2/(F_k - F_j), with F = r^(-alpha-2), (i,j,k) cyclic and lam real, nonzero and otherwise free. The conditions are then also sufficient for self-similar motion, and 2 pi Re kappa = -lam A2, where A2 = ±2 Area is signed. So every scalene shape carries a unique circulation ratio and collapses in exactly one orientation. Isosceles shapes and the equilateral shape carry no finite nonzero admissible circulations. The vortex opposite the middle side is the one whose sign differs from the other two.
results.evidence: Necessity: H(t) = lambda^-alpha H(0) and L proportional to lambda^2, with both conserved. Parametrization: sum_{j<k} Gamma_j Gamma_k x_i = Gamma1 Gamma2 Gamma3 sum x_i/Gamma_i, so the vector (1/Gamma_i) is proportional to u x (uF), with u_i = r_i^2. Sufficiency: in u-space, the velocity du/dt is orthogonal to grad L and grad H because both are conserved, and u itself is orthogonal to both by Euler's theorem because L = H = 0. So du/dt is parallel to u unless grad L is parallel to grad H, which happens only at the equilateral shape. Hence the shape is preserved; conservation of linear impulse fixes z_c, and homogeneity makes the motion self-similar for all time. The rate identity du_i/dt = (Gamma_i A2/pi)(F_j - F_k) comes from Biot-Savart. SymPy verifies L = H = 0 and the common rate -lam A2 (identities.py [1]-[3]). Biot-Savart at 50 digits on random shapes with alpha in {0, 0.3, 1, 1.7} gives a self-similarity residual <= 1e-50 (t1.py).
results.novelty_risk: High for the conditions: Badin-Barry 2018, Reinaud-Dritschel-Scott 2022 and Chen & Liu, Physica D 470 (2024) 134392 (necessary and sufficient conditions and 'explicit exact expressions'; abstract only, full text blocked). Moderate-high for the explicit shape-to-circulation formula, which is likely in Chen-Liu 2024 or JPSJ 90 124401 (2021), both unread.

results.statement: Closed forms for the rates and for P. For every self-similar three-vortex configuration of the alpha-model, 2 pi Im kappa = (1/2) sum_{j<k} (Gamma_j + Gamma_k) r_jk^(-alpha-2). That is, the rotation rate is half the sum of the rates the three pairs would have in isolation. Moreover P = |S|/(8 Area), with S = sum_cyc r_i^2 coth(beta ln(r_k/r_j)) and beta = 1 + alpha/2. For alpha = 0 this reads P = sum_{i<j} u_i u_j (u_i-u_j)^2/(8 Area |prod_{i<j}(u_i-u_j)|) with u = r^2. Geometric reading: the Heron form 16 Area^2 = 2 sum u_i u_j - sum u_i^2 makes shape space a hyperbolic plane. The vector c_i = coth(...) satisfies sum_{i<j} c_i c_j = -1, so sqrt(1+4P^2) = cosh d, where d is the hyperbolic distance from the shape to the geodesic c . u' = 0.
results.evidence: SymPy identities for arbitrary (u, F) with Gamma_i = lam u_i/(F_k - F_j): the rate Im kappa computed from each of the three sides equals the half-sum formula; that equals -(lam/2) S; and the coth identity holds (identities.py [4]-[6]). Numerical checks: the coth formula against direct Biot-Savart on 210 random shapes with alpha in {0, 0.2, 0.7, 1, 1.3, 2, 5}, max relative difference 4.5e-49 (sformula.py). The half-sum formula against Biot-Savart on 100 shapes, 6.5e-41 (omega_num.py). At alpha = 0 the formula matches the paper's P(theta) for mu = 1/2 on 229 values of theta to 1.5e-48, and reproduces the paper's minimum 1.0647059762712043.
results.novelty_risk: The alpha = 0 case is presumably equivalent to Aref 2010 Eqs. (25a)/(25d) (Omega and tau via side lengths), which were read earlier in this project but whose exact form I could not re-check. The half-sum identity may be known. The coth form for general alpha was not seen in any summary. Reinaud-Dritschel-Scott 2022, Chen-Liu 2024 and the JPSJ papers are unread and could contain equivalent rate formulas.

results.statement: MAIN THEOREM (sharp winding bound in the alpha-models). Let alpha > -0.896; this includes every alpha >= 0: Euler at alpha = 0, SQG at alpha = 1, and all 0 < alpha < 2. Every self-similar collapse of three point vortices with kernel r^-alpha satisfies P > sqrt(3+alpha)/(2+alpha). Equivalently, each vortex travels more than (4+alpha)/(2+alpha) times its initial distance to the collision point, its spiral angle exceeds arccos((2+alpha)/(4+alpha)), and |omega_0| t_c > 2 sqrt(3+alpha)/(2+alpha)^2. The constant is sharp and not attained. The infimum is approached as the smallest side rho -> 0 with r1^2 = r3^2 (1 + rho m*), m* = sqrt(2/(1+beta)). In that limit two weak opposite vortices form a dipole near a strong vortex, and the dipole axis makes the angle arccos(1/sqrt(2(1+beta))) with the line to the strong vortex. Here beta = 1 + alpha/2. Values of P_min: 0.8660254 = sqrt(3)/2 (alpha = 0), 0.8012336 (0.25), 0.7483315 (0.5), 0.7041788 (0.75), 2/3 (SQG), 0.6343239 (1.25), 0.6060915 (1.5), 0.5811865 (1.75), sqrt(5)/4 = 0.5590170 (2). P_min is strictly decreasing, continuous at alpha = 0, and tends to 0 as alpha -> infinity. The path ratio runs 2, 9/5, 5/3, 11/7, 3/2 for alpha = 0, 0.5, 1, 1.5, 2. The spiral angle runs 60, 56.25, 53.13, 50.48, 48.19 degrees.
results.evidence:
The proof uses A2-A3. Order the sides r2 = rho < r3 = 1 < r1; this is allowed because P is symmetric in the sides. Write r1^2 = 1 + rho m with 0 < m < 2 + rho and rho < 1; then Area = (rho/2) sin psi with 2 cos psi = rho - m. Put X = rho^(2beta), Y = (1+rho m)^beta and b = (beta/2) ln(1+rho m). Then S = (1+rho m)(1+X)/(1-X) + rho^2 coth b - (Y+X)/(Y-X).
(i) Since Y > 1, (Y+X)/(Y-X) <= (1+X)/(1-X), so S >= rho m + rho^2 coth b.
(ii) coth b > 1/b. The lemma 1/ln(1+x) >= 1/x + 1/2 - x/12 holds for all x > 0: g(x) = 12x/(12+6x-x^2) - ln(1+x) has g(0) = 0 and g'(x) = x^3(24-x)/((12+6x-x^2)^2 (1+x)) >= 0 below the root 3+sqrt21 of 12+6x-x^2, and beyond that root the right side is negative. Hence S > (rho/beta) Lam, with Lam = beta m + 2/m + rho - rho^2 m/6 > 0.
(iii) Exact identity: Lam^2 - (1+2beta)(4-(m-rho)^2) = ((1+beta)m - 2/m - rho)^2 + (rho^2/3)(1 + 6beta - beta m^2 - rho m + rho^2 m^2/12). This is positive. If m < 2, the bracket exceeds 2beta - 1 > 0. If m >= 2, then (1+beta)m - 2/m - rho >= 2beta, so the square is >= 4beta^2, while the bracket term is >= -(2+3beta)/3; and 12beta^2 - 3beta - 2 > 0 for beta > 0.552.
Therefore P = S/(4 rho sin psi) > Lam/(4 beta sin psi) > sqrt(1+2beta)/(2beta) = sqrt(3+alpha)/(2+alpha).

results.statement: New proof of the Euler bound. At alpha = 0 (beta = 1), A4 gives a short proof that every self-similar three-vortex collapse has |omega_0| t_c > sqrt(3)/2, sharp. The proof uses only the side-length formula for P and three elementary inequalities: no mu-parametrization, cubic Q, discriminant or resultant. It proves only the global bound, not the per-mu minima of Theorem 1 of the paper.

results.statement: Near-limit expansion. result.depth_assessment:
This is a substantive and clean result, not a numerical table. P_min(alpha) has the exact form sqrt(3+alpha)/(2+alpha), and the path-length ratio is (4+alpha)/(2+alpha). The proof is short, elementary and checked step by step. It unifies the Euler case with the SQG and generalized-Euler models, and it gives a far simpler proof of the paper's Corollary 1. The key structural facts are: every scalene shape carries exactly one admissible circulation ratio; the rotation rate is half the sum of the pair rates; and P is a symmetric coth expression in the side lengths with no circulations left in it. Together these turn the problem into an inequality about triangles.

Caveats. The collapse conditions are certainly known, and the parametrization and rate formulas are likely in unread 2021-2024 papers. The bound applies to self-similar collapses only: gSQG also has non-self-similar collapse when H is nonzero, and there P is not a single constant. The result is about a geometric property of an idealized model, so its physical significance is moderate. It is a natural companion or extension section for the existing paper, not a separate major theory.

result.direction: DIRECTION 4 (label: geometry): the geometry behind sqrt(3)/2. result.summary: The main result is a closed formula for P that covers every self-similar three-vortex collapse. The circulations enter through a single angle psi, defined by tan psi = 3 sqrt3 |G1 G2 G3| / |(G1-G2)(G2-G3)(G3-G1)|. The shape enters through its latitude lambda on Kendall's shape sphere, which is the Weitzenboeck ratio: sin lambda = 4 sqrt3 Area / (s12^2 + s13^2 + s23^2). With these, P = (2 - cos^2 lambda -/+ cos psi cos lambda) / (sin psi sin 2 lambda); the minus sign belongs to the collapsing arc whose collinear end has the weaker like-signed vortex in the middle. The formula is proved as an exact SymPy identity against the paper's rate lemma and checked by Biot-Savart for 1960 configurations with random circulations (relative error 5e-36 at 40 digits). The geometric reason: on Kendall's sphere, H is the potential of charges G_jG_k (total charge zero) at the three binary-collision points; the zero-impulse set is the meridian orthogonal to their dipole moment; and at every self-similar configration the complex gradients of H and of the angular impulse L are proportional, dbar H = (i kappa/2) dbar L. That proportionality makes the spiral angle beta = arctan 2P equal to the angle between grad H and the zero-impulse circle. So Theorem 1 says the level curves of H cross the zero-impulse circle at less than pi/6. From the formula, the paper's Theorem 1 follows in a few lines. P > sqrt3/2 is a single Cauchy-Schwarz step, (1+S)^2 - (1-S)(1+3S) = 4S^2. The arc minima solve the Chebyshev-type cubic 2c^3 - 3c +/- cos psi = 0 (c = 1/cos lambda), and eliminating c gives back the paper's Q(mu,y). The monotonicity in mu follows from the envelope theorem. The constant sqrt3/2 is a Regiomontanus maximal-angle problem: pi/2 - beta is the angle subtended at e^{i psi} by the real segment [s, s^3], and as psi -> 0 this tends to arctan(2x/(1+3x^2)) <= pi/6. Physically, the mu -> 0 limit is a strong vortex capturing a weak vortex dipole; the minimizing triangle tends to angles (0, 2pi/3, pi/3), with the dipole's self-propulsion speed equal to the swirl speed and its axis at 60 degrees. At mu = 1 the minimizer has angles (pi/8, 5pi/8, pi/4), and arccos(1/3) = 2 arcsin(1/sqrt3), twice its latitude. That relation holds only in the symmetric case, not in general. The closest prior work is Gallay-Sverak 2026 (arXiv:2609.10847, read locally). They have H harmonic in the shape variable, the zero-impulse circle, the complex rate and the winding coefficient s (= P), but they do not state the angle identification, the normal form or any minimization. Gröbli 1877, Section 10 may contain the normal form in other variables; I could not read it (the host is blocked).

results.statement: Every self-similar collapse of three point vortices (G1G2+G2G3+G3G1=0, L=0) satisfies P = |omega_0| t_c = (2 - cos^2 lambda + eps cos(psi) cos(lambda)) / (sin(psi) sin(2 lambda)). Here lambda in (0, pi/2) is given by sin lambda = 4 sqrt3 |Area| / (s12^2+s13^2+s23^2), the Weitzenboeck ratio, which is the latitude on Kendall's shape sphere (equator = collinear shapes, poles = equilateral). psi in (0, pi/2] is given by tan psi = 3 sqrt3 |G1G2G3| / |(G1-G2)(G2-G3)(G3-G1)|, and psi = pi/2 when two circulations are equal. Equivalently |sin 3 theta_g| = sin psi and |cos 3 theta_g| = cos psi, where theta_g is the polar angle of (1/G1, 1/G2, 1/G3) in the plane sum = 0, measured from (1,-1,0). eps = -1 on the collapsing arc whose collinear endpoint has the like-signed vortex of smaller |Gamma| in the middle, and eps = +1 on the other arc. For G = (1, mu, -mu/(1+mu)): cos psi = (1-mu)(2+mu)(1+2mu)/(2R^{3/2}), sin psi = 3 sqrt3 mu(1+mu)/(2R^{3/2}), R = 1+mu+mu^2, and eps = -1 on the paper's arc A_- when mu < 1. In Mercator form, cosh eta = 1/cos lambda: P = (cosh 2eta - k cosh eta)/(2 sin psi |sinh eta|) with k = -eps cos psi.
results.evidence: Proof, two routes. (i) Exact identity: from the paper's positions, S = 2r^3(2r+(1-m)cos th)/(1+m)^4 and Area = -r^3 sin th/(2(1+m)^3). Hence sin lambda = sqrt3(1+m)|sin th|/D0 and the signed cos lambda = M(C)/D0 with D0 = 2r+(1-m)cos th, using D0^2 - 3(1+m)^2 sin^2 th = M(C)^2. So the paper's collapse factor M(C) is the signed cosine of the latitude. The paper's P(theta) = N/(2 mu r M sin theta) then equals the master formula iff 9(1+m)^2 N(C) = 2r^4(2D0^2 - M^2) + 2r^4 cos(psi) M D0, which SymPy verifies exactly. results.statement: Consequences of G1, proved without the paper's cubic. (a) P > sqrt3/2 for every self-similar three-vortex collapse. This needs (1 + sin^2 l)^2 > cos^2 l (1 + 3 sin^2 l), whose difference is 4 sin^4 l, and cos psi + sqrt3 sin psi sin l <= sqrt(1+3 sin^2 l) by Cauchy-Schwarz. (b) P_- < P_+ pointwise in lambda when 0 < psi < pi/2. On the eps = +1 arc P >= (2 - cos^2 l)/sin 2l >= sqrt2, with equality only at psi = pi/2. (c) On each arc the unique critical point solves 2c^3 - 3c + k = 0, where c = cosh eta = 1/cos lambda and k = cos psi (arc P_-) or -cos psi (arc P_+). The trigonometric solution is c = sqrt2 cos(phi), cos 3phi = -k/sqrt2. The minima are P_-/+ = (2c^2+1) sqrt(c^2-1) / (2 sin psi). (d) Rational parametrization of both minima by C = c^2: cos^2 psi = C(2C-3)^2, P^2 = (2C+1)^2 / (4(8C - 4C^2 - 1)), cos^2 beta_min = (8C - 4C^2 - 1)/(12C). C in [1, 3/2] gives P_- and C in [3/2, (2+sqrt3)/2) gives P_+. Also cos beta_min = sin psi / (sqrt3 sinh 2 eta*), and the minimizer latitude satisfies 3cos^2 l* - 2 = cos psi cos^3 l*. Eliminating C: cos^4 psi + 108 cos^2 psi X^3 - 108 cos^2 psi X^2 + 18 cos^2 psi X - 2 cos^2 psi + (9X-1)^2 = 0 with X = cos^2 beta_min. (e) dP_-/dpsi = 4(1-x^2)^2 / (x^3 sin^2 psi sin 2l*) > 0 (x = cos l*, envelope theorem), and psi increases strictly with mu on (0,1] (d log sin psi/d mu = (1+2mu)(1-mu)(2+mu)/(2mu(1+mu)R) > 0). So P_- increases strictly from sqrt3/2 (psi -> 0) to sqrt2 (psi = pi/2), and P_+ decreases strictly to sqrt2.
results.evidence: Every algebraic step is verified in SymPy (s4_sympy.out): the critical-point numerator 2c^3-3c+k; 2c^2-1-kc = (c^2-1)(2c^2+1) at the critical point; P^2 in terms of C; the cos^2 beta_min formula; the Cauchy-Schwarz polynomial 4S^2; the envelope sign 4(x-1)^2(x+1)^2/x^3. The link to the paper: Res_C[C(2C-3)^2 - cos^2 psi, 4 sin^2 psi y - (2C+1)^2(C-1)] = 46656 mu^2 (mu+1)^2 R^9 * Q(mu,y), so these minima are exactly the roots of the paper's cubic. Only the proofs (Cauchy-Schwarz, the Chebyshev cubic, the envelope argument) and the rational parametrization are. Their novelty risk is tied to G1: if Gröbli's Section 10 already has the normal form, the Cauchy-Schwarz proof is still not found in any source read.

results.statement: For any N vortices, a configuration moves self-similarly (dz_j/dt = kappa (z_j - z_c)) iff dbar H = (i kappa / 2) dbar L as vectors in C^N, with L = sum G_j |z_j - z_c|^2. For three vortices with G1G2+G2G3+G3G1 = 0, this passes to the shape sphere (any conformal chart, e.g. w = (z3-z1)/(z2-z1), or Kendall's sphere). There H = Re h is harmonic with logarithmic poles of charge G_jG_k at the three binary-collision points (total charge 0, which is the harmonic condition), and kappa = -i conj(h'(w)) / (|z2-z1|^2 d ell/d wbar) on the zero-impulse circle. Consequently the spiral angle beta = arctan(2P) equals the angle between grad H and the zero-impulse circle, and the level curves of H cross that circle at angle pi/2 - beta. Invariant restatement of Corollary 1: for every circulation triple, the level curves of the three-vortex Hamiltonian meet the zero-impulse circle on the shape sphere at an angle smaller than pi/6. The sup, pi/6, is approached as mu -> 0. At mu = 1 the maximal crossing angle is arcsin(1/3).
results.evidence: Proof: Gamma_j dz_j/dt = -2i dH/dzbar_j (Biot-Savart), and dL/dzbar_j = Gamma_j (z_j - z_c). Both H and L are invariant under translations and rotations, and at L = 0 their differentials vanish on the dilation and rotation directions. The shape map is holomorphic, so dbar passes to the quotient: H_wbar = (i kappa/2)|z2-z1|^2 ell_wbar at ell = 0. Write dH = -(Im kappa/2) d ell - (Re kappa/2) d ell o J, with |grad ell| = |J grad ell|. Then tan(angle between grad H and the tangent J grad ell) = |Im kappa|/|Re kappa| = 2P. Numerics: in the w-plane, tan of that angle equals 2P to 40-digit precision (ratio 1.0) at 33 shapes for mu in {0.3, 0.5, 1} (s2_shapeangle.out). In Kendall's stereographic chart: s5_more.out part 1.
results.novelty_risk: Moderate to high as a statement. Gallay-Sverak 2026 (arXiv:2609.10847, read locally, Sect. 5 and App. E) have H = w + wbar with w holomorphic in zeta, the Casimir circle, the complex rate lambda in Eq. (E.1), and the fact that the level sets of H cross the circle transversally (Prop. 5.4). The angle identification follows from those in a few lines, but I did not find it stated there or elsewhere. The complex-gradient identity is essentially O'Neil 1987's and Gallay-Sverak's Eq. (5.12) characterization of collapse configurations. O'Neil (AMS host) could not be read.

results.statement: Kendall-sphere normal form. The binary-collision points c_jk lie on the equator, 120 degrees apart. Since s_jk^2 = (S/3)(1 - n.c_jk), H = -(1/4pi) sum G_jG_k ln|xi - xi_jk|^2 + const in stereographic coordinates xi, and L = 0 is the meridian orthogonal to the dipole moment V = sum G_jG_k c_jk. Rotate so the meridian is the real axis. The charges sit at rho omega^k with Re(sum q_k rho omega^k) = 0, and with Sigma q = 0 and e1 = e2 = 0 one gets h'(s) = -(iv/2pi)(s - tau)/(s^3 - tau), tau = rho^3 = e^{i psi}. Hence, for real s = e^eta, 2P = |Re X|/|Im X| with X = (s - tau)/(s^3 - tau). So pi/2 - beta is the angle subtended at the unit-circle point e^{i psi} by the real segment [s, s^3]. The other arc uses e^{i(pi-psi)}. As psi -> 0 with eta = x psi, P -> (1+3x^2)/(4x), so tan(pi/2 - beta) -> 2x/(1+3x^2) <= 1/sqrt3. This is a Regiomontanus maximal-angle problem with maximum pi/6 at x = 1/sqrt3, and it is the source of sqrt3/2. Locally (blow-up at the (2,3)-collision point) H becomes Re(zeta + log zeta), a point charge in a uniform field, and the zero-impulse circle becomes the bisector Re zeta = 1/2. The minimizer is at zeta = e^{i pi/3}, the apex of an equilateral triangle on the charge and its mirror point.
results.evidence: The Regiomontanus form is algebraically equivalent to the eta form of G1: divide Re and Im of (s - tau)(s^3 - taubar) by s^2. The psi -> 0 limit (3t^2+1)/(4t) is a SymPy limit (s4_sympy.out). Numerics: a direct construction of the stereographic chart (xi = (w - e^{i pi/3})/(w - e^{-i pi/3}), rotated perpendicular to V) gives s real to 1e-40, |cos arg tau| = cos psi to 5e-51, and the subtended angle equals pi/2 - beta to 1.8e-49 over mu in {0.02, 0.3, 0.5, 0.9, 1} (s5_more.out part 1).
results.novelty_risk: The electrostatic picture of H on the shape sphere and the Hopf/Kendall reduction are standard: Montgomery for three bodies; Gallay-Sverak and Anurag-Goodman for vortices. The factorization h' ~ (s - tau)/(s^3 - tau), the angle psi and the Regiomontanus reading were not found in any source read. Low-to-moderate risk, with evidence limited as in G1.

results.statement: As mu -> 0 (G = (1, mu, -mu/(1+mu))), the minimizer of P on A_- tends to the degenerate triangle with angles (A, B, C) -> (0, 2pi/3, pi/3) at (strong vortex, weak positive, weak negative). A ~ (sqrt3/2) mu, |z2 - z3| ~ mu |z1 - z3|, and the collision point tends to the strong vortex. In cotangent form, along the self-similar family (cot B - cot C = sigma, sigma < 0), P -> (1 + 3 sigma^2/4)/(2|sigma|) = (2 - cos alpha)/(2 sin alpha), alpha = 2B - pi, which is minimal (sqrt3/2) at sigma = -2/sqrt3. The limit is not a two-vortex-plus-tracer problem. It is a strong vortex capturing a weak dipole: X = pair centre, delta = (z3 - z2)/mu, reduced system conj(Xdot) = (1/2pi i)(1/X + 1/delta), conj(deltadot) = (1/2pi i)(1/delta - delta/X^2). Its self-similar solutions are exactly Re(delta/X) = 1/2 (zero impulse), with P = (3/4 + v^2)/(2|v|), v = Im(delta/X). The minimizer has |delta| = |X| (self-propulsion speed = swirl speed) and the dipole axis at 60 degrees to the line of centres. The pair's net circulation mu^2/(1+mu), forced by the harmonic condition, rotates the dipole at the same order as the strain. Without it there is no self-similar collapse, only rigid collinear rotation.
results.evidence: The limit shape is proved rigorously. The constraint mu(3t^2-1) + 2t sigma(mu-1) - sigma^2 = 0 (t = cot C) has a root analytic in mu near 0 for fixed sigma != 0 (implicit function theorem), so P_mu -> P_0 uniformly on compact sigma-intervals. Theorem 1(a) gives a unique critical point, which traps the minimizer near sigma = -2/sqrt3. Numerics: at mu = 1e-6, A = 4.96e-5 deg, B = 119.99998, C = 59.99998, |z2-z3|/(mu|z1-z3|) = 0.9999993, A/((sqrt3/2)mu) = 0.9999995 (s5_more.out part 5; table in s1_intrinsic.out). The dipole system is derived by formal leading-order asymptotics (not a rigorous limit theorem). Its self-similar family and P formula are exact for the reduced system and agree with the rigorous limit. The no-net-circulation claim was checked by hand algebra (only Im w = 0, w in {0, -1/2} survive).
results.novelty_risk: LKZ 2000 and Gallay-Sverak discuss dipole scattering and near-collapse at mu = 1 or for scattering. The capture-limit P formula and the 60-degree / equal-speed characterization of the infimum were not found in the sources read. Moderate risk that the limit shape is noted somewhere.

results.statement: At mu = 1 (G = (1,1,-1/2), psi = pi/2) the minimizing triangles have angles (pi/8, 5pi/8, pi/4), with cotangents (1+sqrt2, 1-sqrt2, 1) and sigma = -sqrt2. Their Kendall latitude is lambda* = arcsin(1/sqrt3), so the colatitude is the 'magic angle' arccos(1/sqrt3). beta_min = arccos(1/3) = 2 lambda*, the spherical distance between the minimizer and its mirror image. This is the equality case cos alpha* = b/a = 1/a of the paper's Lemma with b = 1 in 2P = (3 - cos 2 lambda)/sin 2 lambda, and it is not structural. The same b = 1 coincidence holds in the mu -> 0 blow-up (a = 2), but beta_min = 2 lambda* fails for mu < 1: as mu -> 0, lambda* -> 0 while beta_min -> pi/3. The value 1/3 is the maximum of sinh eta / cosh 2 eta, i.e. 1/3 = cot^2(pi/3), set by the 120-degree spacing of the binary-collision points. No tetrahedron is involved. result.reasoning:
I checked this independently with my own derivation and my own code. I read only the explorer's sphere_core.py, to confirm the conventions: J = sum Gamma_i x_i, S = sum Gamma_i, L = sum_{i<j} Gamma_i Gamma_j |x_i - x_j|^2, M = sum_{i<j} Gamma_i Gamma_j, and n = unit((x2-x1)x(x3-x1)). All my files are in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-GENChase/04604b4b-7efe-5ca6-9b53-4838030930e5/scratchpad/research/check-S1-structure/: sym_check.py, num_static.py, num_traj.py and num_edge.py, with outputs in out_sym.txt, out_static.txt, out_traj.txt and out_edge.txt.

HAND PROOF (my own; it agrees with the one given).
(a) S^2 - |J|^2 = sum_{i<j} Gamma_i Gamma_j |x_i - x_j|^2 = L. M = 0 forces S != 0, because S^2 = sum Gamma^2 + 2M > 0; the stated proof leaves this implicit. So |p| = 1. The weights Gamma_i/S sum to 1, so p lies in Pi and therefore on Pi intersected with the sphere, which is the circumcircle.
(b) Write x_i = c + xi_i with xi_i perpendicular to n. Then x_j x x_i = d n x (xi_i - xi_j) + xi_j x xi_i, so dx_i/dt = d u_i + nu_i n, where u_i is the planar Biot-Savart velocity in Pi with orientation n. Identity N is just a scalar triple product, [n x (xi_i - xi_j)].xi_i = -n.(xi_j x xi_i), which gives nu_i = -u_i.xi_i.
Planar self-similarity from M = 0 and L = 0: Groebli's side-length equations make the chord shape stationary iff Gamma1(X3-X2) = Gamma2(X1-X3) = Gamma3(X2-X1). When M = 0 this solution set is a 2-plane on which L vanishes, so it is exactly {L = 0}. I also checked this symbolically below. The chord plane's L equals the sphere's L because the distances are the same. Substituting u = alpha w + beta n x w and using |w|^2 = -2 rho w.a on the circle gives nu_i = rho(alpha w.a + beta w.b') = [rho(beta a - alpha b') x w].n, which is exactly the stated s and Omega. At no point is there a division by d. Three distinct points on a sphere are never collinear, so rho > 0.
(c) dp/dt = 0 because sum Gamma_i w_i = 0. The velocity field is therefore an infinitesimal similarity fixing p, so d ln l_ij/dt = s for every pair and dn/dt = Omega x n = -rho(alpha a + beta b'). Since p = d n + rho a, this gives d(n.p)/dt = -rho^2 alpha and Omega.p = d^2 beta + rho^2 beta = beta. Take e_perp = rho n - d a; then p x e_perp = -b', and the azimuthal rate is (dn/dt).(-b')/rho = beta. kappa scales as 1/length^2 and rho as length, so ahat and bhat depend only on the constant chord shape (and on the Gamma_i and the orientation). Under reversal of orientation, d and alpha both flip, while s and Omega do not change.

SYMPY (sym_check.py; every residual is exactly 0):
- the cross-product split, in the WLOG frame n = e3;
- identity N;
- planar self-similarity. With Gamma = (1, mu, -mu/(1+mu)), which is general for M = 0 up to scale, z1 = 0, z2 = 1, z3 = x + iy: the real and imaginary parts of the numerators of u_i w_j - u_j w_i all reduce to 0 modulo the planar L = 0 polynomial;
- the frame identity d u + nu n = s w + Omega x w for arbitrary d and rho;
- the (c) identities Omega x n, d(n.p)/dt = -rho^2 alpha, Omega.p = beta, and azimuthal rate = beta.

NUMERICS
- Instantaneous check (num_static.py, 60 digits): 800 configurations from two seeds, built directly on the sphere with no planar parametrization. x1 and x2 are random, and x3 is on the L = 0 circle. Gamma is any M = 0 triple, randomly permuted and scaled, with mu in (-30, 30); 265 cases have mu < 0. The set includes 146 tiny triangles with rho < 1e-2 and covers d in (-1, 1), with about half of the cases having d < 0. Worst-case residuals:
  - |p| - 1 and p in Pi: 2e-61
  - kappa spread across i: 4e-49
  - (b) residual relative to |v|: 2.4e-48
  - chord rate vs s: 4.6e-49
  - dn/dt formula: 2e-54
  - d(n.p)/dt + ahat: 7e-57
  - Omega.p - beta: 5e-61
  - azimuthal rate - beta: 2e-48
  - dp/dt: 1e-61
- Edge cases (num_edge.py, 50 digits):
  - d = 0 exactly (vortices on a great circle, L = 0): every identity holds to about 1e-50, and the chord rates are exactly 0.
  - Equilateral chord triangles, which are relative equilibria: the formulas hold with alpha of about 1e-52, so the 'not a relative equilibrium' hypothesis is not actually needed.
- Trajectories:
  - num_traj.py (scipy DOP853, rtol 1e-13): 12 random cases, each integrated from about d = -0.9 through d = 0 to about d = +0.9. Throughout: p is fixed to 1e-15; the chord shape is constant to 1e-11; ahat and bhat are constant to 3e-10 relative; d(t) = d0 - ahat t to 7e-11; rho(t) = sqrt(1 - d(t)^2) tracks the chord scale; and the azimuth of n equals psi0 + (bhat/ahat)(atanh d0 - atanh d(t)) to 8e-9.
  - mpmath odefun (Taylor, 30 digits) with mu = 1/2 over t in [0, 0.8]: ahat, bhat, the linear law for d and p are all constant to 2e-31.

I found no flaw, and the statement holds exactly as written, including for d <= 0.

Minor caveats:
- S != 0 needs M = 0, which the proof does not mention.
- 'Chord shape constant' should be read as 'up to similarity, with orientation preserved'.
- The 'cos(beta)' in the verbal summary is d = n.p, not the beta_k of kappa.
- An aside I verified numerically but did not prove separately: since d is linear in t, every such motion runs from d = -1 to d = +1 (or the reverse). The configuration emerges from a collision and ends in a collision, with total duration 2/|ahat|. This follows from (c) and may already be known.

Novelty: I did not search the literature. The statement is elementary once the split x_j x x_i = d(...) + (normal term) is written down, so a Kidambi-Newton 1998 priority risk remains plausible, as the explorer notes.

result.summary: For an exact self-similar collapse, every consequence of the bound on turns, rotation angle, arclength, curvature or swept area only restates it, because the motion is an exact logarithmic spiral. These are listed below with their sharp constants and labelled as restatements. The substantive result concerns motions that do not collapse. When a collapse is perturbed so that the angular impulse L is nonzero, the triple scatters from a collapsing shape w_in to an expanding shape w_out. The rotation of z2 - z1 between the two instants where |z2 - z1| = l is exactly (P_in + P_out) ln(mu l^2/(R|L|)) + C + O(|L|/l^2). The proof is an exact reduction to a planar shape flow with a circle of fixed points; C is an explicit convergent integral. It follows that every close three-vortex encounter rotates at a log-rate c = P_in + P_out > sqrt(3). The infimum sqrt(3) is sharp and is not attained. So each time the regularization length is divided by a factor below e^(pi/sqrt3) = 6.13, the configuration makes at least one more full turn after the collapse. This puts a number on Gallay-Sverak 2026, who show that collisions can be regularized only up to rotation: P is the log-frequency of that non-selection. The same law holds, numerically, under kernel smoothing (coefficient 4P per ln(1/eps)), for two concentric rings (coefficient 2P >= 2F_n) and under additive noise. Under additive noise L is a martingale and ends Gaussian, and the law of the post-collapse orientation is log-periodic in the noise level. Its first circular moment has modulus sech(pi c/2)^(1/2) < 0.3621, so under this noise model the full, rotation-including zero-noise limit cannot exist. SDE runs with 6000 samples confirm this within Monte Carlo error. A secondary result: in the co-rotating, co-shrinking frame the tracer flow is autonomous with constant positive divergence. At least N-1 exact self-similar fluid particles fall into the collision point on the vortices' spiral, and at most 5N-5 stagnation points exist. For (d) the bound implies nothing about the energy, the stability exponents or the enstrophy.

results.statement: Take Gamma = (1, mu, -mu/(1+mu)) with 0 < mu <= 1 (mu > 1 follows by the swap symmetry), R = 1+mu+mu^2, u = z2-z1, w = (z3-z1)/u, and g(w) = 1 + 2 mu Re w - (1+mu)|w|^2. Take any motion with angular impulse L != 0 whose scale-invariant energy h is not H(w*), where w* = 1/(1+mu) is the stationary collinear equilibrium, and is not the value of H at one of the four relative equilibria on the zero-impulse circle C = {g = 0}. Suppose further that its level curve {H = h} meets C. Then the shape orbit is a heteroclinic arc from a collapsing shape w_in in C to an expanding shape w_out in C, with H(w_in) = H(w_out) = h. The motion exists for all t, with |u| -> infinity as t -> +-infinity. The rotation Phi(l) of arg u between the first and last instants at which |u| = l satisfies Phi(l) = (P_in + P_out) ln(mu l^2/(R|L|)) + C_arc + O(|L|/l^2) as l^2/|L| -> infinity. Here P_in = P(w_in), and P_out = Im a(w_out)/(2 Re a(w_out)) is the winding number of the mirror-image collapse conj(w_out). C_arc = int_{-inf}^0 (Im a - Im a_in) dtau + int_0^inf (Im a - Im a_out) dtau + P_in c_in + P_out c_out, where ln|g(w(tau))| = lambda_in tau + c_in + o(1) as tau -> -infinity and ln|g(w(tau))| = -lambda_out tau + c_out + o(1) as tau -> +infinity. There are two possible exits. w_out = conj(w_in) is the mirror channel, which is always the exit for L < 0. The other possibility is w_out = conj(w_2), where w_2 is the second collapsing shape with the same h; this cross channel occurs for L > 0 exactly when h exceeds H at the higher collinear equilibrium, which is Gallay-Sverak's threshold.
results.evidence: PROOF. Biot-Savart homogeneity gives du/dt = a(w) u/|u|^2 and dw/dt = b(w)/|u|^2, with a and b evaluated at z = (0,1,w). The conserved quantities are L = (mu/R)|u|^2 g(w) and the scale-invariant H(w). (i) Conservation of L gives the identity grad g . b = -2 Re(a) g for every w. (ii) b = 0 on C (the paper's Lemma 3). Off C, b = 0 only at w*, because a relative equilibrium with L != 0 must have omega L = gamma2/(2 pi) = 0 and so be stationary, and the only stationary configuration is w = 1/(1+mu). (iii) Differentiating (i) on C shows that grad g is a left eigenvector of Db with eigenvalue -2 Re a. Db also has eigenvalue 0 along C, so C is normally hyperbolic away from the four relative equilibria. (iv) If grad H were parallel to grad g at a point of C where Re a != 0, then grad g would be orthogonal to the right eigenvector, which is impossible. So level sets of H cross C transversally there; Gallay-Sverak Prop. 5.4 gives the same conclusion by another route. (v) H = c1 ln|w|^2 + c2 ln|w-1|^2 with c1, c2 > 0 tends to -infinity at w = 0 and w = 1 and to +infinity at infinity, and its only critical point is w*. So {H = h} is a compact union of smooth closed curves on which b vanishes only on C. Each arc between two points of C is therefore one orbit, running from a normally repelling point (collapse) to a normally attracting point (expansion). Conjugation maps expanding shapes to collapsing shapes and preserves H and P. The channel assignment follows from Gallay-Sverak Sect. 5.2, with their Casimir C proportional to -L. (vi) With dtau = dt/|u|^2 one has Phi = int Im a dtau, and |u|^2 = L R/(mu g). Near w_in, |w - w_in| is comparable to |g| along the arc, which gives the stated expansions of ln|g| with errors O(|g|). Integrating yields the formula with error O(eps), eps = R|L|/(mu l^2). NUMERICS. The reduced shape flow was integrated with mpmath odefun at 30-32 digits, with eps0 = 1e-10, 1e-14 and 1e-16, giving C to about 1e-17 (batch_C.log). mu = 1 has an independent closed-form reduction: dphi/dx = (4 Lam x^2 + (x-s)(2x-s))/(2x sqrt([4 Lam x^2 - (x-s)^2][(2x-s)^2 - 4 Lam x^2])), with x = |u|^2/(3|L|), s = sign L, Lam = s13 s23/s12^2, and P = (2Lam+1)/sqrt((4Lam-1)(4-4Lam)), which reproduces the paper's Groebli form. Tanh-sinh quadrature of this formula agrees with the ODE to 2e-19 and 2e-17 for the two channels. Direct double-precision (DOP853) Biot-Savart integration of perturbed collapses, not using the reduction, was run for mu = 1/2 with delta = 1e-4..1e-8. The rotation minus (c ln(1/eps) + C) falls in proportion to delta, to 6.4e-8 in the mirror channel and 7.2e-6 in the cross channel at delta = 1e-8. The increment per decade is 4.903152 against c ln10 = 4.903152, and 9.661784 against 9.661837. For mu = 1 both signs converge to the quadrature constants to 1e-6. Values: mu = 1 at the minimizer, c = 2 sqrt2, C = -0.92777862110072644 (L > 0) and 0.73991322408055712 (L < 0). mu = 1/2 at the minimizer, mirror channel: c = 2.1294119525424087, C = -0.29741263363270831. results.statement: Model: additive independent Brownian noise sigma dB_j on each vortex, with each real coordinate having variance sigma^2 dt. This may not be Grotto-Romito-Viviani's noise. (a) Under the harmonic condition, L is a martingale with zero Ito drift, because sum Gamma_j^2 = (sum Gamma)^2. At the encounter L is approximately N(0, sigma^2 V) with V = 2 t_c sum_j Gamma_j^2 |z_j(0) - z_c|^2, so the two channels are equally likely. (b) The post-collapse orientation is Theta_sigma = c ln(1/sigma) - c ln|Z| + const (mod 2 pi) with Z ~ N(0,1). Its law is asymptotically log-periodic in sigma with period 2 pi/c in ln sigma. Its first circular moment has modulus sech(pi c/2)^(1/2) and phase c ln(1/sigma) + const. The unreduced zero-noise law therefore has no limit; only its law modulo rotation converges. (c) By C2, sech(pi c/2)^(1/2) < sech(sqrt(3) pi/2)^(1/2) = 0.3621, and this is the sharp supremum of the non-uniformity.

results.statement: Passive tracers in an exact self-similar N-vortex collapse (Re kappa < 0). (i) With xi = (x - z_c)/(lambda e^(i phi)) and s = int dt/lambda^2, tracers obey dxi/ds = W(xi) = conj(F(xi)) - kappa xi, with F(xi) = (1/(2 pi i)) sum Gamma_k/(xi - xi_k). This is an autonomous flow with constant divergence 1/t_c > 0. (ii) W has no periodic orbits and no separatrix cycles. (iii) Zeros of W solve conj(xi) = F(xi)/conj(kappa), so there are at most 5N-5 of them (Khavinson-Neumann). A zero is a saddle if |F'| > |kappa| and a repelling node or focus if |F'| < |kappa|. In the nondegenerate case, #saddles - #repellers = N - 1 by Poincare-Hopf (index +1 at infinity and +1 at each vortex), so there are at least N - 1 saddles. (iv) A fluid particle reaches z_c at t_c if and only if its xi-orbit is bounded, that is, if it is a zero of W or lies on a saddle's stable manifold (a finite union of curves). Every other particle converges to a point x_inf != z_c. (v) Each zero is a fluid particle that moves exactly on the vortices' logarithmic spiral. For N = 3 this means at least two such particles with winding P > sqrt(3)/2, each travelling sqrt(1+4P^2) > 2 times its initial distance. Swallowed particles approach z_c asymptotically along the same spiral.
results.evidence: Proof. (i) is direct substitution. (ii) The flux of W across a closed orbit equals area/t_c > 0, because point vortices contribute zero flux, which contradicts tangency. (iii) Khavinson-Neumann, Proc. AMS 134 (2006), applied to a rational function of degree N; det DW = |kappa|^2 - |F'|^2 and trace DW = 1/t_c. (iv) In the far field, d|xi|^2/ds = |xi|^2/t_c + O(1/|xi|), so orbits either stay bounded or escape, and escaping ones leave x at a positive distance. Near a vortex the fast rotation averages the radial drift to +r/(2t_c), so orbits cannot accumulate on vortices; this averaging lemma is only sketched. Poincare-Bendixson then applies. Numerics at 50 digits: for 30 configurations (mu in {1, 0.8, 0.5, 0.2, 0.05}, six shapes each), all roots of the degree-10 resolvent polynomial were found and filtered. The index sum was -2 in all 30 cases. Counts were 2, 4 or 6 zeros, with 2-4 saddles and 0-2 repellers, and |F'|/|kappa| was at least 0.046 away from 1. At the least-winding collapses for mu = 1 and mu = 1/2 there are exactly two zeros, both saddles. Direct integration of the vortices plus a tracer (mpmath odefun, 30 digits) shows the tracer at a zero moving self-similarly to within 1.4e-21 up to 0.9 t_c. Files: tracers.py, tracers.log, tracer_check.py, tracer_check.log.

(iv) and (v), for the collapse frame, were not found. The link to P is trivial.

results.statement: Restatements of P > sqrt(3)/2 (sharp, not attained) for any exact three-vortex collapse or burst. (1) Shrinking by a factor s rotates the configuration by 2P ln s > sqrt(3) ln s: more than 0.6347 turns per decade, or 68.8 degrees per halving. A burst sweeps the same angle while growing by s, and winds infinitely often over [t_c - eps, t_c], though P > 0 alone already gives that. (2) z_j - z_c is proportional to (t_c - t)^(1/2 - iP); the complex exponent has |arg| > pi/3, and trajectories are 1/2-Hoelder in time. (3) Curvature at distance r from the collision point is 2P/(r sqrt(1+4P^2)) > sqrt(3)/(2r), and the radius of curvature is below (2/sqrt3) r. Paths have finite length r0 sqrt(1+4P^2) > 2 r0 but infinite total curvature. (4) The radius to z_c sweeps area P r0^2/2 > (sqrt3/4) r0^2, and sum_j Gamma_j A_j = (P/2) L = 0. (5) The turning angle of any body-fixed direction, including the circumcenter and mutual separations, obeys the same law.
results.evidence: Each item follows directly from z_j(t) - z_c = lambda e^(i phi)(z_j(0) - z_c), with lambda^2 = 1 - t/t_c and phi = -P ln lambda^2, together with the paper's Corollary 1. Log-spiral curvature is 1/(r sqrt(1 + b^2)) with b = 1/(2P). These are restatements, not new content.

results.statement: The bound implies nothing interesting for (d). H is constant along collapse and is a separate function of shape. Sum Gamma_j |dz_j/dt|^2 = |kappa|^2 L = 0 and sum Gamma_j z_j^2 = 0 hold identically, independent of P. The linear instability of collapse under L-perturbations has normal eigenvalue -2 Re a in tau-time, so the relative deviation of L grows like 1/(t_c - t) for every shape, whatever P is. Point-vortex enstrophy is infinite. For finite cores (Reinaud-Dritschel-Scott 2022), the only prediction is heuristic: incoming rotation of at least P ln 4 per halving of the core size, with no rigorous content and no data to test it against, since that paper reports no rotation angles.

result.depth_assessment: Honest verdict. Everything about exact collapses in (a), (b) and (c) is a restatement of P > sqrt(3)/2, because the motion is an exact logarithmic spiral; C8 lists those restatements. The one consequence with new content is C1 and C2: P governs the logarithmic rotation of every perturbed (non-self-similar) near-collapse, and so it is exactly the log-frequency of the rotational non-uniqueness after collapse. Gallay-Sverak (2026) proved that collisions can be regularized only up to rotation; the bound turns this into a sharp universal rate: log-rate > sqrt(3), one extra turn per factor below 6.13 in the regularization length, and a noise-law non-uniformity below 0.362. Mathematically the proof is a standard asymptotic analysis of a heteroclinic arc in an integrable planar reduction, so this is a solid, verified, modest extension, not a deep new theory. Its interest lies in connecting the paper's number to the current non-uniqueness and regularization literature. The noise statements are numerical and heuristic, and they depend on a noise model that may not be Grotto-Romito-Viviani's. The tracer theorem is structurally interesting, but its link to P is trivial and its index count is probably known in related settings. The bound says nothing about energy, stability exponents or enstrophy.

result.reasoning:
S1 has several parts, and their novelty differs.

(1) Part (a) is known or immediate. KN state that |J| = R is necessary. p = J/S is an affine combination of the x_i, so it lies in the chord plane and hence on the circumcircle; this is the analogue of KAS eq. (40). Reading the collapse point as J/S is also immediate: if all x_i tend to q, conservation gives q = J/S. The note correctly does not claim this part.

(2) The shrink law s = d*alpha, with d(n.p)/dt = -ahat constant, is equivalent to published results. It follows from KN's chord equations, whose rates carry the volume V = 2*(chord area)*d; that factor is the source of their partner states with different collapse times. It is also Borisov-Lebedev's closed form M_k proportional to 1 - (1 - t/T)^2. The note also treats this as known (S2).

(3) Form (b), dx_i/dt = s w_i + Omega x w_i, is nearly automatic. Chord self-similarity, with p fixed and p a fixed affine combination of the x_i, means {x_i, p} moves by similarities of R^3 that fix p. So a generator (s, Omega) exists trivially. The content is its explicit value. The new part is the rotation law: Omega = d beta_k n + rho(beta_k a - alpha b'), Omega.p = beta_k, and the normal n precesses about p at exactly the planar rate beta_k = bhat/rho^2, not slowed by the factor d. Integrated, this gives psi = 2P artanh(d) + const, so the rotation about p per e-fold of chord scale is 2P/d, compared with 2P in the plane. None of these forms appears in any source I could read. They are also absent from every search summary.

The strongest evidence against prior statement is KN's own reported framing. The ledger's earlier read of the 1999 paper and the search summaries both have them saying that each vortex has a distinct angular velocity on the sphere, in contrast with the common angular velocity in the plane. That is true of per-vortex azimuths about J, and S1 agrees with it: the tilted part of Omega makes each vortex's azimuthal rate beta_k plus a term that differs from vortex to vortex. But it indicates that KN did not recast the motion as a single similarity about p with rotation Omega.p = beta_k.

I stay at 'unclear' rather than 'probably unstated' for four reasons. KN 1998 (33 pages) explicitly derives the collapsing trajectories and is unread. KN 1999 'compares [them] with the planar formulas' and I cannot see those formulas directly. Newton's 2001 book and the Borisov-Mamaev 2005 book are unread. And once chord similarity is known, the decomposition takes about a page, so a careful author could have written it down in passing, for example in stereographic coordinates.

If the result is kept, claim only the rotation half: Omega.p = beta_k, precession of n at bhat/rho^2, and winding 2P/d per e-fold. Credit (a) to KAS and the J/S argument, and credit the shrink law to KN and Borisov-Lebedev. The priority caveat for KN 1998, Newton 2001 and Borisov-Mamaev 2005 should stay until one of them is read. A side point for the S-series: Borisov-Lebedev's remark that vortices scattered from one point 'approach in some other point' conflicts with J conservation; burst and collapse occur at the same point J/S.

result.reasoning:
Parts (i) and (iii) are known. The squared-chord law M_k = D_k R^2 (1 - (1 - t/(A R^2))^2) and the burst-to-equator-to-collapse description are in Borisov-Lebedev 1998, which I read. The partner collapse times are in Kidambi-Newton 1999. The single point p follows at once from conservation of J. The cap-area wording and the "chord |n_c - p|^2 is linear" wording are trivial restatements, so they are not new. A paper should credit these sources.

The open question is (ii): the rotation law psi = -2 P0 ln tan(beta/2), read as a loxodrome of the spherical circumcenter with exactly the planar pitch. I did not find it in any source I could read, and no search hit mentions loxodromes or rhumb lines in connection with vortex collapse. But the most likely prior source, Kidambi-Newton 1999, cannot be read here. Its abstract says it derives formulas for the collapsing trajectories and compares them with the planar ones. Once written in terms of the partner times, the rotation is psi = -P0 ln[(t1 - t)/(t2 + t)], because tan^2(beta/2) = (t1 - t)/(t2 + t). A term like that could sit inside KN's per-vortex azimuth formulas without being identified geometrically.

Against that, KN's stated framing points away from this result: no common angular velocity on the sphere, and solutions that are not self-similar in the stereographic plane. That fits a paper that tracked vortex positions (each azimuth equals psi plus a beta-dependent offset) and never isolated the circumcircle pole. Kidambi-Newton 1998 and Newton's 2001 book are also unread.

So the loxodrome and constant-meridian-angle statement is probably not stated as such, but the analytic rotation law may be implicit in KN. I rate the result "unclear", not "probably unstated", and before any priority claim someone must read the KN 1999 full text (ncc8137.pdf).

Correctness: my independent check confirms (i) to (iii). One point needs a wording fix. The "extra rotation 2 P0 ln(2/(1 + cos beta0))" holds when the planar comparison has the same chord triangle at each instant (planar circumradius = sin beta). If the planar spiral is instead matched by the chord |n_c - p|, which follows the same linear time law, the extra rotation is P0 ln(2/(1 + cos beta0)). The statement should name its matching; sympy confirms both values.

Suggested framing: credit (i) and (iii) to Borisov-Lebedev 1998 and Kidambi-Newton 1998/1999, and present (ii) as "not found in the sources we could read", with no name attached.

result.corrected_statement: Let R be the sphere radius, K = 1/R^2, and rho_c = R sin(beta) the Euclidean circumradius of the chord triangle. Let n be the circumcircle pole, oriented so that the chord triangle has its planar-collapsing orientation about n; collapse is then at beta -> 0 and the burst at beta -> pi. psi is the azimuth of n about the collision point p = M/(sum Gamma), and omega = dpsi/dt, which equals the component along p of the instantaneous similarity rotation. It is not any single vortex's azimuth about p: those differ at finite size. With these definitions: (1) |dpsi/d ln l_ij^2| = P0 |sec beta| = P0/sqrt(1 - K rho_c^2) for every pair and in both phases, for beta != pi/2. (2) |omega| (t_c - t) = P0 sec^2(beta/2); in the final phase this is 2 P0/(1 + sqrt(1 - K rho_c^2)), which lies in (P0, 2 P0]. (3) The pole moves on a loxodrome about p with |dpsi/d ln tan^2(beta/2)| = P0, crossing the meridians through p at the angle arctan(2 P0). As unoriented shapes, the chord shapes of spherical three-vortex collapses are exactly the planar zero-impulse shapes minus the collinear ones AND the equilateral ones. The equilateral ones are relative equilibria on the sphere. Equivalently, they are the planar collapsing arcs, oriented about n. Hence at every instant except the great-circle instant beta = pi/2: (1) > (sqrt3/2)/sqrt(1 - K rho_c^2); (2) > sqrt3/(1 + sqrt(1 - K rho_c^2)) in the final phase; (3) > sqrt3/2. Each bound is sharp at every fixed size: it is approached as mu -> 0 and not attained. For fixed mu, the planar minimizing shape attains P_-(mu) times the curvature factor at every size. At rho_c = R/2 with beta = 30 degrees, the floors are 1 and 4 sqrt3 - 6 = 0.92820...
